grand_strategy.reading:
Saudi Arabia is a rich state that has become a front-line state without
changing its aim, which is to buy time for an economy that will outlast oil.
Everything in the card is a trade of one scarce thing for another: US
protection against Israeli normalisation, a Pakistani and Turkish guarantee
against dependence on Washington, the UAE's exit from Yemen against a Houthi
front of its own, a wartime oil price against lost volume and market share.
The Luttwakian pattern is that each safeguard creates the next exposure: the
February 2026 war put Iranian missiles on Ras Tanura and Riyadh, the
answers (strikes in Iraq, an offensive in Yemen) brought the Houthis to the
capital's airport, and the hedges (Makkah pact, Pakistani troops) show a
kingdom unsure that the United States will fight for it. The thaw with Abu Dhabi
(July-October 2026) is tactical, since Yemen's south, Sudan and the Horn
remain contested. Signals that are not rows: the postponement, at Riyadh's
request, of the Hormuz talks between Gulf states and Iran in Sept 2026
(Saudi Arabia would rather the US negotiates than the Gulf legitimises
Iranian control of the strait); Egypt declining the Makkah pact while saying
Gulf security is its own; and the fiscal arithmetic that makes the 2026 deficit look
better only because the war lifts the price. Open gaps in this pass: the
OIC and Arab League as instruments, Afghanistan, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, the
Horn beyond commentary, and an official Saudi source for the Houthi truce
breakdown (reports date the renewed fighting from June or July 2026).
